# `workload_deployer` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/workload-deployer.satz`

## Purpose

One deployer identity per customer team. A Google project of the team's own holds the
service account its pipelines run as and the bucket its states live in, and the account
holds the roles it needs to roll out folders and Google projects under the workload folder
— nothing more.

A team rolls out many Google projects and folders with templates of its own, in OpenTofu or
in Satz, each with its own state; it never runs as the organisation's IaC account. One entry
of `workload_deployers`, `{ name = "platform" group = "gcp-project-admins@example.com" }`,
is one team — bound in the estate, or requested by the team as `contributes_workload_deployers`
in a small pack of its own, checked with `satz check-request` and vendored by pull request.
`name` is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter; `group` is the address
of the group that may become the account; `folder` is the parent the team creates under,
`google_folder.workload_folder.name` unless the entry names another.

PER ENTRY. The team's infrastructure project `{customer_shortname}-deploy-<name>` under
`deployer_project_folder`, billed to the infrastructure billing account, with the APIs a
deployer's calls need. Inside it the account `svc-deploy-<name>` and the state bucket
`{customer_shortname}-deploy-<name>-state`, which the account may write; the group reads the
project and may become the account — that account only.

WHAT THE ACCOUNT MAY DO. On the parent folder, `deployer_folder_roles`: create and manage
folders and Google projects under it, set their IAM and enable their APIs. On the billing
account, `deployer_billing_roles`: link a new project to it. On the organisation,
`deployer_organization_roles` — `roles/browser` and nothing else by default: the interface
looks the workload folder up by its name among the organisation's folders, and that listing
needs `resourcemanager.folders.list` on the organisation; without it the team's plan stops at
the lookup. The three lists are params, so a customer changes the set without a fork.

MORE PARENT FOLDERS. A team that creates under several folders gets one entry of
`workload_deployer_folders` per further parent, `{ name = "platform-shared" deployer = "platform"
folder = "google_folder.shared.name" }`, which grants `deployer_folder_roles` on that folder
to the team's account.

WHO RUNS WHAT. The team's pipeline impersonates `svc-deploy-<name>` and keeps its state in
the team's bucket; the organisation's state is never read — a looked-up value asks the
Google API for the live resource. The account's address is the pattern above; the pack
exports no interface.

NO CLAIM. The teams' identities are workloads, not controls: this pack witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  use_workload_deployer = true

  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  workload_deployers = []
  workload_deployer_folders = []
  deployer_project_folder = ""
  deployer_folder_roles = [
    "roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin",
    "roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin",
  ]
  deployer_organization_roles = [ "roles/browser" ]
  deployer_billing_roles = [ "roles/billing.user" ]
  deployer_group_roles = [
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator",
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountUser",
  ]
}

use "presets/workload-deployer.satz" when use_workload_deployer
```

`use_workload_deployer` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `billing_account_infra` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deployer_project_folder` | The folder the teams' infrastructure projects are created in — the infrastructure folder as `google_folder.infra_folder.name`, another folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation | edit | low | `"google_folder.infra_folder.name"` |

**deployer_project_folder** — It decides the policies the teams' projects inherit. Changing it afterwards moves every live team project between parents.

An empty answer, `""`, is an answer: the organisation itself.

## Requests

What a project may add to this pack's lists, through `contributes_<param>` in a file the estate uses after a reviewed pull request; `satz check-request` checks such a file.

| list | key | fields | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workload_deployers` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `group` matching `[^@: ]+@[^@: ]+`, `folder` | A team that rolls out folders and Google projects: its name, the address of the group that may become its account, and the folder it creates under |
| `workload_deployer_folders` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `deployer` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `folder` | A further parent folder a team creates under: the entry's name, the team's name, and the folder |
